scope: Review the pending LibreCAD MLINE style-timing patch for same-name style-handle mismatches before integrating it into the consumer.

finding.failurePath: The first patch revision compared styleHandle with the cached MLINESTYLE handle only when late-style placeholders were supplied. If a same-named style was already cached when an MLINE callback arrived, the ordinary projection path could use that style despite a different nonzero source handle. The queue predicate also did not classify a cached handle mismatch as unresolved.
finding.impact: The displayed decomposed lines could use offsets from a style that the MLINE did not reference.
finding.evidence: Code-path review of the pending patch and MLINE callback order. No runtime reproduction was run in this slice.

change.queuePredicate: When deferred import is active, a cached same-name style with a different nonzero, non-NoHandle source handle now enters the pending queue along with missing or cardinality-mismatched styles.
change.projectionGuard: The style-handle equality check now applies whenever projection considers a cached style, both for direct callbacks and deferred placeholders.
change.existingRegressionCoverage: The patch's ASCII/Binary late-style test includes a different-handle profile and expects fallback offsets. It does not yet exercise a style cached before the MLINE callback.

validation.head: PASS: git -C ../LibreCAD apply --cached --check <patch> against index at 078aac892287.
validation.worktree: The LibreCAD checkout was not modified; its pre-existing dirty files and untracked data were left untouched.
validation.diffCheck: PASS: git diff --check in the libdxfrw repository.
validation.consumerBuildOrTests: Not run. The pending patch is not applied to the consumer checkout, and the complete bundled consumer build remains a separate P8-D gate.

remaining: Add a regression where the MLINESTYLE callback is already cached before an MLINE carrying a different nonzero style handle, then verify the wrong style is not used.
Apply the reviewed patch in an isolated/current-head consumer worktree, run the focused MLINE filter tests, then check unrelated MLINE/style handling and build the bundled application once.
Keep native GUI qualification waiting for an active display; this review does not promote consumer or DWG support.
